stories.headline: Army Chief reviews LoC security in Kashmir
stories.title: Army Chief reviews LoC security in Kashmir
stories.summary: Srinagar, Sep 25: Chief of the Army Staff (COAS) General Dhiraj Seth on Friday visited forward areas and formations of the Chinar Corps under Northern Command to review operational preparedness and the security situation along the Line of Control (LoC) and in the hinterland. During the visit, the Army Chief was briefed by commanders on the prevailing security situation, operational readiness and ongoing efforts to strengthen military capabilities. According to the Army, General Seth was also briefed on measures taken to maintain a strong security posture along the LoC and ensure preparedness for counter-terrorist operations in the hinterland. Interacting with troops in operational areas, the COAS praised all ranks for maintaining a high level of vigilance. He also highlighted the key focus areas of “VIJAY”, a five-point framework aimed at transforming the Indian Army into a future-ready force capable of responding quickly across the full spectrum of operations. The Army Chief also appreciated the coordination between the Indian Army, civil administration, Central Armed Police Forces, Jammu & Kashmir Police and other security agencies in maintaining peace and stability in the region. During his visit to Tangdhar, General Seth inspected the Advanced Surgical Eye Camp being organised by the Indian Army under Operation Drishti 2026. The camp, which is being held from September 23 to 30, aims to provide specialised eye care to serving personnel, Veer Naris, veterans, their dependents and civilians, particularly those living in remote and difficult-to-reach areas of Jammu & Kashmir. Specialist teams from Army Hospital (Research & Referral), New Delhi, and 92 Base Hospital, Srinagar, are conducting the medical camp. More than 6,000 patients are expected to be screened, while over 400 eye surgeries are planned during the week-long initiative.

stories.headline: U.P. Congress leaders clash with police, detained during protest against Chief Election Commissioner
stories.title: U.P. Congress leaders clash with police, detained during protest against Chief Election Commissioner
stories.summary: The Congress leaders, including State Congress chief Ajay Rai and party workers demanding the resignation of the CEC, were stopped and later detained while trying to march towards the Uttar Pradesh Assembly
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Uttar PradeshCongress unit on Friday (September 25, 2026) held a demonstration against the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, and clashed with the police, demanding accountability from the Commission, adding that fair elections are the foundation of democracy and alleged the people of the country are witnessing the way constitutional norms are being flouted.

The Congress leaders, including State Congress chief Ajay Rai and party workers demanding the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner, were stopped and later detained while trying to march towards the Uttar Pradesh Assembly.
Mr. Rai alleged that the Chief Election Commissioner had played a role in Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s victory in Varanasi and demanded that the election be cancelled.
“Attack on democracy and tampering with the autonomy of constitutional institutions will no longer be tolerated.

As part of the nationwide protest of the Indian National Congress, today a fierce demonstration was held on the streets of Lucknow along with the Uttar Pradesh Congress colleagues against the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar.
Fair elections are the foundation of democracy, but the people of the country are witnessing the way constitutional norms are being flouted.
Congress will continue its fight from the streets to Parliament to protect the rights of the people and democracy.
We are going to organize district-level protests on Monday.
The way heavy police force was deployed on the streets of Lucknow shows that the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government is fully protecting the Chief Election Commissioner.
Our workers were detained during the protest; it shows the dictatorial mindset of the state administration,” told Mr. Rai, to The Hindu.
Mr. Rai and other Congress leaders climbed the barricades and raised slogans, following which a scuffle broke out between them and the police.
The Congress leaders and hundreds of protesting Congress workers were taken to the Eco Garden — a protest site in the State capital, and later released in the evening.

stories.headline: 2020 Delhi riots case: Supreme Court relaxes specific bail condition for about-to-be-married accused
stories.title: 2020 Delhi riots case: Supreme Court relaxes specific bail condition for about-to-be-married accused
stories.summary: Bench reduces Meeran Haider’s mandatory police station appearances from twice a week to once weekly
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (September 25, 2026) partially relaxed a select bail condition for 2020 Delhi riots accused Meeran Haider, reducing his mandatory police station appearances from twice a week to once a week.
The relief comes ahead of his scheduled wedding on October 17.
The court also exempted his appearance before the police station on his wedding day and October 24.

The short hearing before a Bench headed by Justice Aravind Kumar witnessed Additional Solicitor General S.V. Raju crack a “light-hearted” comment that “he [Haider] can get married at the police station”.
Senior advocate Siddharth Aggarwal, appearing for Haider, vocalised his objection to the comment made by the law officer appearing for the NCT of Delhi, the respondent in the case.
“Mr. Raju is right.
He is saying that police stations are now equipped to conduct marriages [weddings] also,” Mr. Aggarwal explained to the Bench, which did not catch the comment.
Mr. Raju downplayed his comment, explaining that it was only said in a lighter vein.
“My learned friend is serious all the time.
He should be jovial also sometimes,” he remarked.

Mr. Haider said he was facing a lot of hardship due to a bail condition requiring him to mark his attendance twice a week, on Mondays and Thursdays between 10 a.m. and noon, before the jurisdictional Delhi police station.
His counsel said the condition was affecting his attempts to get employment as these were both working days.
